akg.name: AKG
akg.history: AKG Acoustics is an acoustics engineering and manufacturing company founded in 1947 by Rudolf Görike and Ernest Plass in Vienna, Austria. The company is part of Harman International Industries, a subsidiary of Samsung Electronics since 2017.

altec-lansing.name: Altec Lansing
altec-lansing.history: Altec Lansing, Inc. is an American audio electronics company founded in 1927. The company produces loudspeakers and associated audio electronics for professional, home, automotive and multimedia applications.

ampex.name: Ampex
ampex.history: Ampex Data Systems Corporation is an American electronics company founded in 1944 by Alexander M. Poniatoff as a spin-off of Dalmo-Victor. The name AMPEX is an acronym created by its founder, which stands for Alexander M. Poniatoff Excellence. Ampex currently operates as a subsidiary of Delta Information Systems with business units focused on digital data storage systems and industrial control systems.

amphion-loudspeakers.name: Amphion loudspeakers
amphion-loudspeakers.history: Amphion Loudspeakers Ltd. is a Finnish company that manufactures home loudspeakers and professional studio monitors. It was founded in 1998 by Anssi Hyvönen. Their product range includes passive speakers, bass extenders, amplifiers, and active monitors.

apogee.name: Apogee
apogee.history: Apogee Electronics is an American manufacturer of audio interfaces, analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog converters, USB & iOS microphones, and audio production software.

arcam.name: Arcam
arcam.history: A&R Cambridge Ltd. (Arcam) is a British manufacturer of hi-fi equipment based in Cambridge, England. It was established in 1976 by science and engineering students from the University of Cambridge. Since July 2017, it has been part of Samsung Electronics through its subsidiary Harman International Industries.

atc.name: ATC
atc.history: ATC is a British audio equipment manufacturer headquartered in Gloucestershire, United Kingdom, serving the professional and home audio markets. Their products include studio monitors, loudspeakers for HIFI, subwoofers, amplifiers and CD players. ATC designs and manufactures all its drivers, crossovers, and amplifiers in-house in the UK.

audioquest.name: Audioquest
audioquest.history: AudioQuest is a company founded in 1980 by William E. Low that provides audio/video cables, digital-to-analog converters, headphones, power-conditioning products, and various audio/video accessories. Based in Irvine, California, the company has offices in the Netherlands and distributes its products to approximately 65 countries throughout the world.

audio-technica.name: Audio-Technica
audio-technica.history: Audio-Technica Corporation is a Japanese company that designs and manufactures professional microphones, headphones, turntables, phonographic magnetic cartridges, and other audio equipment.

ayre-acoustics.name: Ayre Acoustics
ayre-acoustics.history: Ayre Acoustics Inc. is an American manufacturer of high-performance, high-fidelity audio components and systems. The company was co-founded in 1993 by Charles Hansen, Katie Lehr, and Peter Bohacek.

b-and-w.name: B&W
b-and-w.history: Bowers & Wilkins, commonly known as B&W, is a British company that produces consumer and professional loudspeakers and headphones. The company was founded in 1966 in Worthing, West Sussex, England.

bang-and-olufsen.name: Bang & Olufsen
bang-and-olufsen.history: Bang & Olufsen A/S is a Danish high-end consumer electronics company founded in 1925 by Peter Bang and Svend Olufsen. The company designs and manufactures audio products, television sets, and telephones, originating from their design of a radio that could work with alternating current at a time when most radios still ran on batteries.

boesendorfer.name: Boesendorfer
boesendorfer.history: Bösendorfer is an Austrian piano manufacturer founded in 1828 and has been a wholly owned subsidiary of Yamaha Corporation since 2008. The company is notable for producing pianos with 97- and 92-key models in addition to instruments with standard 88 keys.

boulder.name: Boulder
boulder.history: Boulder Amplifiers is a private corporation founded in Boulder, Colorado in 1983 by Jeff Nelson as a manufacturer of high-end, solid state professional audio electronics.

burmester.name: Burmester
burmester.history: Burmester Audiosysteme GmbH is a German manufacturer of high-end audio components based in Berlin-Schöneberg. The company was founded in 1977 by Dieter Burmester, an Austrian-born musician and engineer.

cambridge-audio.name: Cambridge Audio
cambridge-audio.history: Cambridge Audio is a British manufacturer of audio equipment including headphones, audio systems and components.

carver.name: Carver
carver.history: Bob Carver is an American designer of audio equipment based in the Pacific Northwest.

celestion.name: Celestion
celestion.history: Celestion is a British designer and exporter of professional loudspeakers.

clearaudio.name: Clearaudio
clearaudio.history: Clear Audio Electronic GmbH of Germany is a manufacturer of high fidelity audio products formed in 1978, with a primary focus on vinyl turntables and related products such as cartridges. The company is recognized for incorporating transparent acrylic components in their turntables, with more expensive models featuring parallel tracking tone arms rather than pivot-based designs.

creek-audio.name: Creek Audio
creek-audio.history: Creek Audio is a manufacturer of audio equipment.

dali-loudspeakers.name: Dali Loudspeakers
dali-loudspeakers.history: Danish Audiophile Loudspeaker Industries is a Danish manufacturer of high-end loudspeakers founded in 1983 by Peter Lyngdorf. The company targeted its products towards the Hi-Fi community and is best known for its MegaLine series of high-end loudspeakers.

duntech.name: Duntech
duntech.history: Duntech is an Australia-based professional audio loudspeaker manufacturer, researcher, and developer. The company produces audiophile-grade speakers that are positioned as extremely high-end products.

dynaudio.name: Dynaudio
dynaudio.history: Dynaudio is a Danish loudspeaker maker founded in 1977 that builds speakers using only their own drivers.

electrocompaniet.name: Electrocompaniet
electrocompaniet.history: Electrocompaniet is a Norwegian manufacturer of audio products that bases their approach on achieving sound true to live listening experience rather than relying solely on technical measurements and theory. Their amplifiers have been used in recording studios, including Abbey Road Studios.

electro-voice.name: Electro-Voice
electro-voice.history: Electro-Voice (EV) is an American manufacturer of audio equipment, including microphones, amplifiers, and loudspeakers, focused on pro audio applications such as sound reinforcement and commercial and residential audiovisual installations. As a subdivision of Bosch Communications Systems Inc. since 2006, Electro-Voice markets products for use by consumers as well as small or large concert venues, broadcasting, houses of worship, and in retail situations.

epos.name: Epos
epos.history: Epos Ltd is a British loudspeaker company that specialises in home cinema and hi-fi speakers.

focal-jmlab.name: Focal.JMlab
focal-jmlab.history: Focal-JMlab is a French company that has been designing and selling high fidelity audio systems since 1979. Based in Saint-Étienne, the company manufactures loudspeakers for the home, speaker drivers for automobiles, headphones, professional studio monitors, as well as outdoor speakers and systems dedicated to yachts.

genelec.name: Genelec
genelec.history: Genelec Oy is a manufacturer of active loudspeaker systems based in Iisalmi, Finland. The company was co-founded by Ilpo Martikainen and Topi Partanen in 1978 and designs and produces products for professional studio recording, mixing and mastering applications, broadcast, and movie production.

goldring.name: Goldring
goldring.history: Goldring is an audio equipment manufacturing company established in 1906 when the Scharf brothers began manufacturing phonographs in Berlin, Germany. The company relocated to Britain in 1933, where it continued manufacturing cartridges and turntables.

grado.name: Grado
grado.history: Grado Labs is an American audio manufacturer known for hand building high-end dynamic open-back headphones and cartridges in Brooklyn, New York.

grundig.name: Grundig
grundig.history: Grundig is a German brand founded by Max Grundig in 1945, originally based in Fürth, Germany, producing home appliances and consumer electronics. The original company ceased operations in 2003, after which its business divisions were sold separately, with home appliance and consumer electronics operations acquired by Beko Elektronik and Alba plc in 2004 and subsequently coming under Arçelik ownership.

gryphon-audio-designs.name: Gryphon Audio Designs
gryphon-audio-designs.history: Gryphon Audio Designs is a manufacturer of high-end audio equipment located in Denmark. The company is known for their expensive cost-no-object audio equipment, with few updates and product changes compared to their competition.

harbeth.name: Harbeth
harbeth.history: Harbeth Audio Limited is a British manufacturer of high-fidelity loudspeakers based in Lindfield, West Sussex, England. The company was founded in 1977 by Dudley Harwood, who was previously a Senior Engineer in the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) Research Department.

harman-kardon.name: Harman Kardon
harman-kardon.history: Harman Kardon is a brand owned by Harman International Industries, a wholly owned subsidiary of Samsung Electronics. The brand was originally founded in Westbury, New York, in 1953 by business partners Sidney Harman and Bernard Kardon.

infinity.name: Infinity
infinity.history: Infinity Systems is an American manufacturer of loudspeakers founded in Los Angeles in 1968. Since 1983, Infinity has been part of Harman International Industries, which became a subsidiary of Samsung Electronics in 2017.

jbl.name: JBL
jbl.history: JBL is an American audio equipment manufacturer headquartered in Los Angeles, California, founded in 1946 by James Bullough Lansing, an American audio engineer and loudspeaker designer. The company serves the home and professional audio markets, offering home products including speakers and car audio, as well as professional products such as live PA systems, studio monitors, and cinema loudspeakers. JBL is a subsidiary of Harman International, which is owned by Samsung Electronics.

jmlab.name: JMlab
jmlab.history: Focal-JMlab is a French company that has been designing and selling high fidelity audio systems since 1979. Based in Saint-Étienne, the company manufactures loudspeakers for the home, speaker drivers for automobiles, headphones, professional studio monitors, as well as outdoor speakers and systems dedicated to yachts.

kef.name: KEF
kef.history: KEF is a British company founded in Maidstone, Kent in 1961 by BBC engineer Raymond Cooke. The company produces high-end audio products including HiFi speakers, subwoofers, architecture speakers, wireless speakers and headphones. In 1992, the Hong Kong–based Gold Peak Group acquired KEF through its member company GP Acoustics, and KEF continues to manufacture its products in Maidstone.

kharma-loudspeakers.name: Kharma Loudspeakers
kharma-loudspeakers.history: Kharma International B.V., usually known as Kharma, is a high-end audio equipment manufacturer that produces mainly loudspeakers and cables.

klipsch.name: Klipsch
klipsch.history: Klipsch Audio Technologies is an American loudspeaker company based in Indianapolis, Indiana. Founded in Hope, Arkansas, in 1946 as 'Klipsch and Associates' by Paul W. Klipsch, the company produces loudspeaker drivers and enclosures, as well as complete loudspeakers for high-end, high-fidelity sound systems, public address applications, and personal computers.

klh.name: KLH
klh.history: KLH Audio is an American audio electronics company based in Denver, Colorado. Originally founded in 1957 as KLH Research and Development Corporation in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the company takes its name from the initials of its founders: Henry Kloss, Malcolm S. Low, and Josef Anton Hofmann.

lexicon.name: Lexicon
lexicon.history: Lexicon is an American company that engineers, manufactures, and markets audio equipment as a brand of Harman International Industries. The company was founded in 1971 with headquarters in Waltham, Massachusetts, and offices in Salt Lake City, Utah, before being acquired by Harman in 1993.

linn.name: Linn
linn.history: Linn Products is an engineering company that manufactures hi-fi and audio equipment. Founded by Ivor Tiefenbrun in Glasgow, Scotland, in 1972, the company is best known as the manufacturer of the Linn Sondek LP12 turntable.

lyngdorf-audio.name: Lyngdorf Audio
lyngdorf-audio.history: Danish Audiophile Loudspeaker Industries is a Danish manufacturer of high-end loudspeakers founded in 1983 by Peter Lyngdorf. The company targets its products towards the Hi-Fi community and is best known for its MegaLine series of high-end loudspeakers.

lyra.name: Lyra
lyra.history: Lyra is a series of MP3 and portable media players developed and sold by Thomson Consumer Electronics Inc. under its RCA brand in the United States and Thomson brand in Europe, starting in 1999. In January 2008, Thomson sold its Consumer Electronics division including the RCA brand and Lyra line to AudioVox.

magnepan.name: Magnepan
magnepan.history: Magnepan is a private high-end audio loudspeaker manufacturer located in White Bear Lake, Minnesota, United States. The company's loudspeaker technology was conceived and implemented by engineer Jim Winey in 1969.

manley-labs.name: Manley Labs
manley-labs.history: Manley Laboratories, LLC is an American manufacturer of pro audio and high-end audio equipment located in Chino, California.

martin-logan.name: Martin Logan
martin-logan.history: MartinLogan is a Canadian/US company that produces subwoofer speakers as well as floor-standing, wall-mounted, and in-wall hybrid speakers using electrostatic loudspeaker and planar magnetic thin film loudspeaker technology.

meridian.name: Meridian
meridian.history: Meridian Audio is a consumer audio and home theatre equipment manufacturer based in the United Kingdom, founded in 1977 by Bob Stuart and Allen Boothroyd under the name Boothroyd-Stuart. The company adopted the Meridian brand name in 1985 when it released a CD player, and later developed the lossless compression format Meridian Lossless Packing in 1998 and the lossy Master Quality Authenticated format in 2014.

mobile-fidelity-sound-lab.name: Mobile Fidelity Sound Lab
mobile-fidelity-sound-lab.history: Mobile Fidelity Sound Lab is a record label specializing in the production of audiophile releases. The company is recognized for sourcing nearly all its releases from original tapes and reissues seminal albums on numbered-edition vinyl LP records and hybrid Super Audio CDs, with a catalog encompassing more than 600 albums.

musical-fidelity.name: Musical Fidelity
musical-fidelity.history: Musical Fidelity is a British producer of hi-fi audio equipment founded in the United Kingdom in 1982. The company focuses on streaming music players and amplifiers of various types, and has also produced headphones, digital-to-analog converters, CD players, Bluetooth receivers, and all-in-one systems. They are known for their unusual industrial design, Nuvistor tube use, and Class-AB amplifiers.

nad.name: NAD
nad.history: NAD Electronics is a brand name of an electronics firm whose products include home hi-fi amplifiers and related components.

nagra.name: Nagra
nagra.history: Nagra is a Swiss brand of portable audio recorders first introduced in 1951. In 1997, the company expanded into new markets by launching a range of high-end equipment designed for the audiophile community.

naim-audio.name: Naim Audio
naim-audio.history: Naim Audio Limited is a British hi-fi manufacturer based in Wiltshire, United Kingdom.

nakamichi.name: Nakamichi
nakamichi.history: Nakamichi Corp., Ltd. was a Japanese consumer electronics brand that gained prominence from the 1970s onwards for audio cassette decks. Nakamichi is now a subsidiary of Chinese holding company Nimble Holdings.

nordost.name: Nordost
nordost.history: Nordost Corporation is an American high-end audio company founded in 1991 by Joe Reynolds, Vincent Garino, and Jeffrey Garino and based in Holliston, Massachusetts. The company manufactures and sells audio and video cables, interconnects and audio accessories, with products distributed in 72 countries.

now-hear-this-nht.name: Now Hear This (NHT)
now-hear-this-nht.history: NHT Loudspeakers is an American loudspeaker and audio component company based in Benicia, California, founded by Chris Byrne and Ken Kantor in December 1986.

onkyo.name: Onkyo
onkyo.history: Onkyo Corporation was a Japanese consumer electronics company that specialized in premium home cinema and audio equipment, including AV receivers, surround sound speakers and portable devices. It was active as an independent company from 1946 to 2022, but remains active as a trademark brand under joint operation by Sharp Corporation and Voxx International.

ortofon.name: Ortofon
ortofon.history: Ortofon A/S is a Danish manufacturer of electronic audio equipment and the world's largest producer of magnetic cartridges for phonograph turntables, with 500,000 cartridges sold annually.

polk-audio.name: Polk Audio
polk-audio.history: Polk Audio, Inc. is an American manufacturer of audio products headquartered in San Diego, California, best known for its home and automobile speakers. The company produces a wide range of audio products including amplifiers and FM tuners, and has introduced smart speakers for Google Assistant and Amazon Alexa. In 2006, the company was acquired by Directed Electronics.

proac.name: ProAc
proac.history: ProAc Limited is a British loudspeaker manufacturing company.

proceed.name: Proceed
proceed.history: Madrigal Audio Laboratories was founded in 1984 by Sanford Berlin, when he took over the high-end audio company Mark Levinson. Proceed was one of the brands under Madrigal, alongside Audioaccess, Madrigal, and Imaging. In 1997, the subsidiary Revel Audio was founded for high-quality loudspeakers.

pro-ject-audio.name: Pro-Ject Audio
pro-ject-audio.history: Pro-Ject Audio Systems is a manufacturer of audiophile equipment founded in 1991 by Heinz Lichtenegger and located in Mistelbach, Austria. The company designs its products in Austria and produces them in plants located in Germany, Czech Republic, and Slovakia.

ps-audio.name: PS Audio
ps-audio.history: PS Audio, Inc. is an American company specializing in high-fidelity audio components for audiophiles and professional audio applications. The company manufactures audio amplifiers, preamplifiers, power-related products, digital-to-analog converters, streaming audio devices, and loudspeakers.

quad.name: Quad
quad.history: Quad Electroacoustics is a British manufacturer of hi-fi equipment based in Huntingdon, England. The company is part of the IAG Group, with corporate headquarters located in Shenzhen, China.

rega.name: Rega
rega.history: Rega Research Ltd. is a British audio equipment manufacturer founded in 1973, with its name formed from the initials of its two founders. The company is widely known for their turntables, cartridges and tonearms, and has produced amplification and speakers for over 20 years, while also serving as an original equipment manufacturer for other companies such as NAD and Rotel.

revel.name: Revel
revel.history: Revel is an American manufacturer and distributor of high-end luxury audio loudspeakers based in Stamford, Connecticut. Since 2002, the company has been owned by Harman International Industries, which became a subsidiary of Samsung Electronics in 2017.

revox.name: Revox
revox.history: Revox is a brand name registered by Studer on 27 March 1951 for Swiss audio equipment.

roksan.name: Roksan
roksan.history: Roksan is a British manufacturer of high fidelity audio products for domestic use, based in Rayleigh, Essex. The company is best known for its influential and innovative design for hi-fi equipment, particularly its Xerxes platform for playing LP records.

rotel.name: Rotel
rotel.history: Rotel is a family-owned Japanese manufacturer of hi-fi audio and video equipment including home theater, amplifiers, and compact disc players. The company was started by Tomoki Tachikawa in Tokyo, Japan in 1957 as a hi-fi electronics manufacturer and is currently run by his nephew, Peter Kao.

shure-corporation.name: Shure Corporation
shure-corporation.history: Shure Inc. is an American corporation that specializes in developing and manufacturing audio equipment technology. It was founded by Sidney N. Shure in Chicago, Illinois, in 1925 as a supplier of radio parts kits. The company became a manufacturer of consumer and professional audio-electronics including microphones, wireless microphone systems, discussion systems, mixers, and digital signal processing, as well as listening products including headphones, high-end earphones, and personal monitor systems.

slim-devices.name: Slim Devices
slim-devices.history: Slim Devices, Inc. was a consumer electronics company based in Mountain View, California, founded in 2000. The company's main product was the Squeezebox network music player, which connected to home ethernet or Wi-Fi networks to stream digital audio to stereos, and the company was originally notable for supporting open-source software through their SlimServer software.

snell-acoustics.name: Snell Acoustics
snell-acoustics.history: Snell Acoustics was an American manufacturer of high-end loudspeakers founded by Peter Snell in Massachusetts in 1976. The company was purchased by Boston Acoustics in 1995 and ceased manufacturing in May 2010.

sonos.name: Sonos
sonos.history: Sonos, Inc. is an American audio equipment manufacturer headquartered in Santa Barbara, California. The company was founded in 2002 by John MacFarlane, Craig Shelburne, Tom Cullen, and Trung Mai.

spendor.name: Spendor
spendor.history: Spendor is a British loudspeaker manufacturing company founded in 1969 by audio engineer Spencer Hughes and his wife Dorothy. The company is located in East Sussex, and its name was derived from the first names of both founders.

stax.name: Stax
stax.history: Stax Ltd. is a Japanese company that makes high-end-audio equipment, best known for their electrostatic and electret headphones called earspeakers. In December 2011, Chinese audio equipment company Edifier acquired 100% equity in Stax.

tannoy.name: Tannoy
tannoy.history: Tannoy is a British manufacturer of loudspeakers and public address systems founded in 1926. Today the company is part of the Music Tribe group of brands.

tara-labs.name: Tara Labs
tara-labs.history: TARA Labs is a manufacturer of high-end audio cables based in Medford, Oregon, and is currently led by president Merrill Bergs. The company is known for their use of solid wire in their products.

teac.name: TEAC
teac.history: TEAC Corporation is a Japanese electronics manufacturer created by the merger of the Tokyo Television Acoustic Company, founded in 1953, and the Tokyo Electro-Acoustic Company, founded in 1956.

technics.name: Technics
technics.history: Technics is a Japanese audio brand established by Matsushita Electric in 1965. Since its establishment, Matsushita has produced a variety of HiFi and other audio products under the brand name, including turntables, amplifiers, radio receivers, tape recorders, CD players, loudspeakers, and digital pianos. The brand was originally conceived as a line of high-end audio equipment to compete against brands such as Nakamichi.

thiel-audio.name: Thiel Audio
thiel-audio.history: THIEL Audio was an American privately held high performance loudspeaker manufacturer founded in Lexington, Kentucky, and later based in Nashville, Tennessee. All products were designed and built in their 35,000-square-foot facility in Lexington, with distribution to over 30 countries. Thiel ceased operations in 2018.

thorens.name: Thorens
thorens.history: Thorens is a formerly Swiss manufacturer of high-end audio equipment historically renowned for producing phonographs and turntables. In addition to audio playback equipment, Thorens has also been a manufacturer of harmonicas and Swiss-made cigarette lighters.

tivoli-audio.name: Tivoli Audio
tivoli-audio.history: Tivoli Audio Inc. is an American company that produces radios. It was founded in 2000 by Tom DeVesto and Henry Kloss.

vac.name: VAC
vac.history: Valve Amplification Company (VAC) is a U.S. supplier of high end audio electronics principally utilizing vacuum tube technology. It was founded in 1990 by Kevin Hayes and Channing W. Hayes, and as of 2011 is located in Sarasota, Florida.

western-electric.name: Western Electric
western-electric.history: Western Electric Export Corporation is a manufacturer of vacuum tubes and high-end audio gear based in Rossville, Georgia. The company traces its roots to 1872 with the Bell Telephone Company and the original Western Electric, and was started as a successor in 1995 when AT&T granted Charles G. Whitener a license to the trademark and intellectual property of the original Western Electric company.

wharfedale-loudspeakers.name: Wharfedale Loudspeakers
wharfedale-loudspeakers.history: Wharfedale is a British audio equipment brand best known for loudspeakers. It is currently part of the International Audio Group.

wilson-audio.name: Wilson Audio
wilson-audio.history: Wilson Audio Specialties Inc. is an American high-end audio loudspeaker manufacturing company located in Provo, Utah. The company was co-founded by David A. Wilson and his wife Sheryl Lee Wilson in 1974, with David Wilson serving as Chairman of the Board until his death in 2018 and Sheryl Lee Wilson serving as Vice Chair.

wilson-benesch.name: Wilson Benesch
wilson-benesch.history: Wilson Benesch is a British private company that designs and manufactures hi-fi audio equipment, including loudspeakers and turntables. The company was founded in 1989 in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England, and operates its entire design and manufacturing operation from Falcon House, an art-deco styled building built in the 1930s.

zu-audio.name: Zu Audio
zu-audio.history: Zu Audio is an audiophile loudspeaker and cable manufacturer located and established in Ogden, Utah.
